alternative_architecture.description: Reorganize around one feature-delivery transaction rather than a hierarchy of global planning and evidence systems. State: keep product canon/design decisions separate from pipeline policy and repository inventory; use a small approved feature contract, Git commit/tree, and one append-only attempt journal as the principal records. Planning: a human selects priority, then one bounded planning/impact pass identifies relevant requirements, files, tests, and unresolved decisions just in time. Execution: a restartable state machine moves one worktree through selected → implementing → validating → human review → merged/blocked, using one write-capable coding worker initially. Validation: task-specific Git scope checks, Unity compilation/tests, clean-tree verification, fresh semantic review when useful, and explicit human Play Mode criteria produce one gate report attached to the candidate commit. Recovery: preserve the worktree, commit, failed gate results, retry count, and next action; measure progress by resolved gates and relevant diffs, not merely any changed file. GDD change: create a reviewed change event mapping stable requirement IDs to affected contracts, tests, and implementation surfaces; replan or revalidate only those affected. Unity: use an actual Editor/host runner, in-memory or temporary test assets, committed-scene conformance checks, meta preservation, and mandatory human visual/feel review. Reconciliation becomes an occasional audit/migration tool; RAG remains optional navigation; GER becomes the bounded retry policy inside the delivery state machine; provider adapters remain replaceable plumbing.
alternative_architecture.why_better: This preserves the mechanisms that fixed real project failures—bounded workers, runtime feedback, clean Unity validation, repair limits, Git isolation, and human qualitative authority—while removing repeated identity/provenance transformations from the critical path. It also gives evolving canon a scoped impact model and makes merged player value, lead time, retries, and human effort measurable.

structured_output.architecture_summary: The architectural kernel is sound: durable repository state, bounded workers, deterministic supervision, Git isolation, runtime evidence, bounded repair, and human design/feel authority are appropriate for autonomous Unity development. The current composition is not sound enough as an autonomous system. Its implemented layers stop at task inspection, conformance bookkeeping, and read-only provider invocation; selection, write execution, Unity validation orchestration, recovery, readiness, and integration are disconnected or absent. It is also overbuilt relative to demonstrated gameplay throughput and models evolving canon with overly broad hashes plus undercomplete manual surface lists.
structured_output.biggest_uncertainty: No real gameplay task has traversed the proposed production path, and no production revalidation exists. Consequently, the largest unknown is the human and bookkeeping cost per repeated Unity feature—not whether individual schemas and adapters pass their isolated tests.

evidence.observation: At the frozen commit, the read-only commands `taskcontrol validate`, `taskcontrol ready`, and `taskcontrol state` showed a structurally valid 37-contract graph, unavailable readiness, zero dispatch authority, NSC-023 conformant, and NSC-003 not delivered. The working tree stayed clean.
The active runtime still lacks repository writes, approved command execution, production orchestration, task selection, GER integration, Unity execution, and Git integration.

NSC-003 claims to be a concrete single-agent contract while the current-state document separately lists seven unresolved input, steering, arrival, pathing, and restriction decisions. The contract is therefore not a safe autonomous handoff as written.

NSC-003 and fourteen other contracts still contain evidence or locks for the deleted nested DoorPrototype scene. The shared resource registry also locks that obsolete path, yet `taskcontrol validate` passes because validation checks resource-key consistency rather than repository existence.

The GDD still declares the deleted nested scene authoritative and calls `Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity` a noncanonical stub. The current implementation, scene-location check, and NSC-023 evidence instead identify `Assets/Scenes/DoorPrototype.unity` as authoritative.

Despite that semantic contradiction, NSC-023 derives as conformant because the evaluator checks the unchanged whole-GDD hash, current contract hash, and an explicitly enumerated surface list—not semantic agreement between those sources or completeness of the surface set.

The NSC-023 evidence record uses the new authoritative scene while its task contract's bootstrap evidence still names the obsolete scene, demonstrating internal authority drift immediately after the scene move.
A previous static validator passed the door implementation, but human Play Mode testing found that the progress bar did not visually update because the generated Filled Image lacked a sprite.

The camera passed static evaluation twice but failed in Unity because it faced the wrong direction, did not follow the player, and later framed the door incorrectly. Structured human runtime feedback enabled repair.

The GER progress guard correctly detected a no-op refinement, but the subsequent pass added a null-target warning and regression test rather than further resolving framing. This shows that requiring any Assets delta can incentivize defensible-looking churn rather than outcome progress.
Earlier builder tests invoked the production Build method, which opened and saved the canonical scene. The later in-memory seam and byte-preservation test corrected that unsafe validation design.

The GDD changed eleven times between August 13 and August 21 and mixes product mechanics with development-agent roles, pipeline coordination, current repository inventory, token policy, packages, and build configuration. A whole-document hash therefore has an unusually large blast radius.

Tracked production-pipeline source, tests, and supporting documents under Pipeline comprise roughly 28,000 lines excluding reconciliation outputs; committed reconciliation outputs add roughly 73,000 lines. The Unity gameplay, scene, and test text under Assets/NoSafeCircle is roughly 1,600 lines.

From August 18 through the frozen August 23 commit, Git history is dominated by reconciliation, task/evidence, testing-policy, and provider-runtime work; Assets received scene/test safety changes but no new gameplay feature after Assignment 6.

gdd_iteration_concerns: Current behavior is asymmetric and unsafe for iteration: any GDD edit makes every evidenced implementation stale because records bind the entire GDD hash, while planned but undelivered contracts remain unchanged unless a human notices and revises them. Implemented work is over-invalidated; planned work can silently remain stale.

The GDD should contain intended game behavior, not mutable repository inventory, provider workflow, token policy, or agent coordination. Those concerns currently make unrelated process edits look like gameplay-canon changes.

Stable requirement identifiers and explicit design-change events are missing. Task contracts cite prose sections, so there is no deterministic causal mapping from an edited decision to affected tasks, tests, assets, or evidence.

When design changes after planning, affected contracts should be revised or superseded before execution. When it changes after implementation, a reviewed impact proposal should open migration/revalidation work only for affected requirements and surfaces. Unaffected evidence should remain current.

Tuning and feel values should be allowed to evolve through playtesting without forcing global reconciliation. The system needs explicit classifications such as invariant, initial tuning value, implementation choice, and human-feel criterion.

The recent canonical scene relocation already demonstrates failed synchronization: implementation and evidence moved, while the GDD, task contracts, resource claims, build contract, and milestone documentation did not move together.
human_intervention_points: Choose product priority; dependency readiness cannot determine which feature creates the most player value.

Approve or clarify underspecified interaction semantics. NSC-003 currently needs decisions about input arbitration, click versus hold, destination replacement, arrival, pathing, and restriction lifetime.
Inspect Unity scenes, prefabs, serialized references, Console output, visual framing, UI readability, animation, input feel, and gameplay feel in Play Mode.
Decide whether a playtest finding is an implementation defect, a tuning change, or a canon/design revision.
Approve architecture changes, new design artifacts, scope changes, and newly discovered substantial prerequisites.
Review and merge changes while automatic integration remains disabled.
Provide or approve visual assets and judge art consistency; source-level tests cannot establish production presentation quality.
Until evidence publication is automated, select which test/runtime artifacts and conformance surfaces genuinely prove each gate.
hypothetical_failure_solutions: Progressive Decomposition and Artifact Authority primarily protect against future distant-work ambiguity and unauthorized AI design. No artifact task or production artifact flow currently exists.
Parallel resource claims, multiple worktrees, merge queues, and GitHub synchronization protect against concurrency and visibility problems that a one-worker project has not reached.
Continuous backlog replenishment and autonomous task claiming protect a future mature delivery system; the current system cannot execute one selected ticket.
Provider interchangeability, capability classes, fallback, and extensive hostile JSON/container validation protect transport/vendor failures more than current game-development failures.

Repeated independent multi-model reconciliation verification protects global bootstrap completeness. It was useful for the one-time seed but is disproportionate for ordinary GDD edits or feature delivery.

A generalized Unity/code scanner and compact top-k context system mostly protect future context-scale concerns. The canonical GDD is only 349 lines, and current documentation already concedes top-k retrieval cannot prove complete canon.
Full Artifact GER, style evaluators, and automated artifact promotion protect future generated-content workflows, not the current blockers in movement, combat, enemies, rooms, and game flow.

next_slice.proof_of_value: A real, visible mouse-directed gameplay behavior must be merged from an isolated worktree within one working day, with no canonical-asset mutation, no unresolved completion gate, no more than two repair attempts, and approximately one hour or less of human hands-on work excluding ordinary playtesting. If the slice instead stalls on orchestration or evidence bookkeeping, that falsifies the near-term leverage claim and identifies the next minimal blocker.
next_slice.title: Feature-first delivery kernel: mouse-directed movement
next_slice.why: If additional infrastructure is forbidden, the first failure is the ambiguous NSC-003 contract and stale scene authority; immediately after that, the machinery has no authorized write/test/repair lane. Delivering a smaller movement slice exercises state, execution, Unity validation, human feedback, repair, and recovery in one transaction while producing actual player value.

observed_failure_solutions: Fresh bounded role invocations and explicit artifact handoffs successfully produced the original door prototype faster than a single long model context and made the static review trail inspectable.
Human Unity feedback plus bounded repair solved the visibly broken door progress indicator that static code/tests missed.
GER's structured runtime-feedback loop solved camera direction, follow, and framing failures that passed semantic/static evaluation.
Circuit-breaker accounting prevented unlimited camera repair attempts.
The no-op detector caught an actual Refiner response that claimed implementation without changing Assets, although its progress definition needs improvement.

The Unity testing policy, in-memory builder seam, committed-scene conformance tests, XML reporting, and clean-tree checks address the actual unsafe pattern where normal tests invoked a production scene-saving entry point.
Persistent task identities and contracts address repeated reconstruction and stale Assignment 5 goal artifacts across sessions.
The production GDD index's source hashes and deterministic rebuild address the actual stale July Assignment 4 knowledge base.
Separating builder capability from serialized scene conformance addresses an observed recurring error: code that can generate an asset is not proof that the committed asset contains it.
Human approval boundaries addressed real scope changes, such as the controls HUD amendment, without silently converting an agent suggestion into canon.
overengineering: The repository built a large reconciliation/verification/refinement system for a one-time 37-record bootstrap, including domain workers, multiple auditor types, selective pass two, streaming field repairs, conflict clustering/arbitration, recovery, and extensive committed output history.

AgentRuntime heavily hardens recursive JSON values, subclass behavior, Windows path aliases, schemas, provider envelopes, usage metadata, atomic publication, and two transports before any production agent can edit gameplay or run Unity.
The 349-line GDD has a roughly 1,900-line production retrieval implementation and test suite, while workers are still expected to receive the whole GDD because retrieval completeness is unproven.

TaskGraph, TaskExecution, AgentRuntime, future ExecutionCrew, reconciliation, Git, Unity evidence, and conformance records each preserve overlapping identity/provenance without one transaction that connects them.
ArchitectureReview became the first real AgentRuntime consumer, proving transport but not the value-bearing risks of repository writes, Unity execution, repair, integration, or moving design.
The roadmap specifies Progressive Decomposition, Artifact Authority, GitHub mirroring, continuous scheduling, and parallelism before measuring one corrected task's delivery cost.
Documentation itself has become another mutable state layer: CURRENT_STATE says Codex migration is active near the top but later calls Codex unimplemented and repeats obsolete next-step instructions.
state_and_authority_concerns: Necessary boundaries are: approved product canon/design decisions; a versioned task/feature contract; integrated Git code/assets; deterministic validation artifacts; human qualitative approval; transient attempt state; and a derived scheduling view.

Task contracts should own intended work only. Git should own integrated implementation. One gate report should own validation evidence. One attempt journal should own transient execution/retry state. Readiness should be a deterministic policy view over those inputs.

Reconciliation snapshot, bootstrap provenance, contract hash, TaskExecution request, AgentRuntime request/result, future crew run, conformance record, and Git history currently repeat identity without an atomic transaction or recovery coordinator.

TaskExecution validates the supplied task path/hash syntactically but does not resolve and verify that identity against committed repository state before invoking AgentRuntime. It is an audit wrapper, not task authority.

The conformance evaluator trusts a manually authored surface list. A relevant omitted file can change without invalidation, while any unrelated GDD edit invalidates the record. This is undercomplete code impact combined with overbroad canon impact.
Invalid evidence is given global precedence for a task, but record immutability and correction/revocation semantics are not a complete operational recovery model.

The GDD currently combines game-design authority, development-process policy, implementation ownership, mutable repository inventory, and build configuration. These should not share one global canon hash.

The scene-location smoke test proves the actual Unity asset path but searches stale references only in Assets C# files. It therefore passes while the operational task/resource graph and GDD remain wrong.
The current `conformant` result proves internal identity/blob consistency for NSC-023, not semantic agreement across all claimed authorities or completeness of the change surface.

Mutable convenience views are acceptable for navigation, but START_HERE, CURRENT_STATE, master context, milestone records, individual ADRs, and DECISIONS currently disagree about active stage and implemented behavior, weakening repository-as-memory.
strong_decisions: A local deterministic process, rather than an LLM context, should own the long-running control loop.
Workers should receive one bounded, approved unit of work and should not rebuild the roadmap.
Agent claims about changed files, commands, tests, or success must not become deterministic evidence.
Runtime and human Unity observations are first-class feedback for interactive and visual work.
Repair attempts require budgets, circuit breakers, and escalation.
No-op attempts must consume budget; the progress measure should be improved to gate resolution rather than any diff.
Task definition, transient execution, integrated code, validation evidence, conformance, readiness, and human approval are correctly recognized as distinct concepts.
Reconciliation should propose reviewed changes rather than directly mutate the living graph.
Repository writing should occur on isolated branches/worktrees, with one worker before parallelism.
Missing design detection should be separate from authority to invent design.
Top-k retrieval is correctly treated as navigation rather than complete canon.
Autonomous dispatch is correctly fail-closed until a real delivery policy exists.
structural_flaws: The proposed hierarchy is not a closed control loop. Implemented code does not connect selected work to authorization, repository writes, Unity execution, repair, evidence publication, dependency readiness, merge, or the next task.

There is no canonical per-attempt aggregate. A future supervisor would need to coordinate several immutable artifact trees and infer which request, worktree, commits, validation, human feedback, and evidence record form one transaction.
Moving canon is treated as snapshot freshness rather than causal change. Whole-document hashing cannot distinguish an unrelated pipeline wording edit from a changed gameplay invariant.
The persistent graph already drifted after the canonical scene move, showing that neither reconciliation, graph validation, nor conformance currently maintains evolving authority.
Contracts marked `single_agent` are not necessarily executable: NSC-003 simultaneously carries that label and unresolved product decisions.
Current conformance can prove internally consistent evidence while task and GDD descriptions contradict the repository.
Evidence publication is manual and occurs after integration, so the path from candidate validation to durable conformance is neither atomic nor restartable.
Progress is not measured in merged player value, elapsed delivery time, human minutes, repair effectiveness, or escaped defects.
The architecture has separate abstractions for generation, evaluation, validation, review, and evidence, but no approved rule for selecting the minimum evaluator set by task risk.

If forbidden to add infrastructure for one slice, failure occurs first at contract ambiguity/stale authority, then at the absence of a write-capable execution and Unity-validation lane—not at missing RAG, decomposition, GitHub, or parallel scheduling.
structured_output.throughput_assessment: Bounded agents have demonstrated useful local coding and repair leverage on the door and camera prototypes. The current production architecture has not demonstrated end-to-end leverage and is presently throughput-negative: five days of heavy pipeline work produced substantial auditability but no new gameplay feature, while readiness and authorization remain disabled. It cannot plausibly turn weeks into days until one feature can be selected, edited, validated in Unity, repaired, reviewed, and merged through a restartable path. Even then, humans remain the bottleneck for design ambiguity, visual assets, feel, balancing, and final integration, so the realistic target is faster implementation cycles—not unattended completion of the whole game.
structured_output.verdict_reason: The approach is not fundamentally wrong, but the current organization is partially unsound. Its strongest control principles are worth retaining; its critical path is fragmented, its evidence model does not handle evolving canon correctly, and its infrastructure investment is far ahead of demonstrated delivery. Reorganize around a minimal feature-delivery state machine, make scoped change impact explicit, and demote reconciliation, RAG, decomposition, artifact machinery, provider interchangeability, and continuous autonomy to optional services justified by observed failures.
